'''''Garamaudo''''' ({{lit|beware the cursed one}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[tethysaurine]] mosasaur known from [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Santonian]] age) rocks of France. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Garamaudo bauciensis''''', known from the fragmentary remains of at least four individuals. It inhabited a [[freshwater]] environment and likely lacked the paddle-like flippers of more derived mosasaurids.

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Bouc-Bel-Air - Sousquières locality (France).png|thumb|left|[[Type locality (biology)|Type locality]] in southeastern France [{{font color|#F8061D|★}}] ]]
The ''Garamaudo'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Aix-en-Provence Basin (Bouc-Bel-Air - Sousquières locality) in [[Bouc-Bel-Air]], [[Bouches-du-Rhône]] department, in southeastern France. The remains of at least four separate individuals are known from this region, housed at the [[Departmental Council of Bouches-du-Rhône]] in [[Marseille]]. The most complete of these is CD13-PAL.2018.3.1–3, 5–15, 18, which comprises around 20 elements of a single individual collected by the [[Museum d'Histoire Naturelle Aix-en-Provence]] in 1997. These include the [[Anatomical terms of location#Anterior and posterior|posterior]] part of the left [[hemimandible]], seven vertebrae (five of which are from the neck), six [[rib]]s, and much of the right [[pelvis]]. Other remains from this outcrop include CD13-PAL.2018.3.1.16, a right [[humerus]] found near the previous specimen but likely belonging to a smaller individual, and CD13-PAL.2018.3.1.4, a dorsal vertebra found near these specimens but belonging to a larger individual than either of them. CD13-PAL.2018.3.4, a dorsal vertebra comparable in size to the first individual, was found in an outcrop {{nowrap|~{{convert|20|m|ft}}}} away.<ref name="Garamaudo" />

In 2026, Nathalie Bardet and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Garamaudo bauciensis'' as a new genus and species of tethysaurine mosasaur based on these fossil remains, designating the most complete individual as the [[holotype]] specimen. The humerus was regarded as a [[paratype]], and the other two vertebrae were treated as referred specimens. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Garamaudo'', is derived from the [[Provençal dialect|Provençal]] expression {{lang|oc|Gara au maudo}}, which means {{gloss|beware the cursed one}}, in turn alluding to Garamaudo, a malicious freshwater-dwelling serpentine creature of local legend. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''bauciensis'', means {{gloss|from Bouc-Bel-Air}}, referencing the type locality.<ref name="Garamaudo" />

== Description ==
{{gallery
|Garamaudo bauciensis (vertebrae).png|Holotype (A–E) and referred (F, {{nowrap|G–I}}) vertebrae
|Garamaudo bauciensis (CD13-PAL.2018.3.1.16, humerus).png|Paratype humerus
|Garamaudo bauciensis (CD13-PAL.2018.3.11, pelvis).png|Holotype pelvis
}}

The lack of clearly distinct sutures on the mandible and pelvis of the ''G. bauciensis'' holotype suggests this individual was skeletally mature at the time it died. The total body length was likely around {{cvt|2.5|m|ft}}, comparable to the closely related ''[[Tethysaurus]]'', which has been estimated as being under {{cvt|3|m|ft}} long. The other named tethysaurine, ''[[Pannoniasaurus]]'', was substantially larger, at up to {{cvt|6|m|ft}} long. The limbs and pelvic girdle of ''Garamaudo'' may have been more [[plesiomorphic]] ('primitive') in morphology in contrast to the derived paddle-like flippers of other mosasaurids. The known ''Garamaudo'' fossils exhibit clear [[osteosclerosis]] (increased bone density), indicating it was likely capable of diving to shallow depths. It may not have been capable of rapid acceleration and maneuverability, instead catching prey by ambush.<ref name="Garamaudo" />

== Classification ==
To test the affinities and relationships of ''Garamaudo'', Bardet et al. (2026) included it in an updated version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Zietlow et al. (2023).<ref name="Zietlow2023" /> It was recovered in an [[polytomy|unresolved]] clade with ''[[Pannoniasaurus]]'', ''[[Tethysaurus]]'', and an unnamed taxon from Villeveyrac-L'Olivet, together forming the subfamily [[Tethysaurinae]]. Tethysaurinae was recovered as the [[sister taxon]] to [[Yaguarasaurinae]], with this clade in a large polytomy of other mosasaurid groups. == Palaeoenvironment ==
The Bouc-Bel-Air - Sousquières locality, from which ''Garamaudo'' is known, represents a [[freshwater]] [[depositional environment]]. During the late [[Cretaceous]] period, this may have been a moderately [[Eutrophication|eutrophic]] lake with periodic flooding events. Other reptiles known from this formation include small indeterminate [[crocodylomorph]]s and a [[bothremydid]] turtle tentatively assigned to the genus ''[[Polysternon]]''. Other fossils from the locality include fish, such as ''[[Atractosteus africanus]]'' (a [[gar]]) and ''[[Axelrodichthys megadromos]]'' (a [[coelacanth]]).<ref name="Garamaudo" />
